record.title: Chi Ma–Ai Diem suspends freight clearance in December 2021
record.region: East and Southeast Asia and Oceania
record.scope: Bilateral cargo clearance at Chi Ma–Ai Diem (Aidian)
record.exceptions: Restored trade was limited by commodity and transloading; this endpoint is first partial cargo movement.
record.enforcement: Gate interviews and provincial figures document actual resumed export/import vehicles.
record.relationship: Distinct from R6-EA-004 and R6-EA-005; December 22 traffic prevents a single continuous December–April spell.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; unknown endpoints are not extended to 21 October 2026.
record.official_rationale: Suspected COVID-19 cases in Ai Diem, as reported by Tuoi Tre. Chi Ma border commander Nguyen Duc Binh also reported both COVID prevention and an Ai Diem customs-network malfunction as explanations for the December 8 halt.
record.context: Separate first Chi Ma spell; actual trade resumed before the January 17 closure.
record.uncertainty: December 22 marks partial trade restoration, not clearance of all stranded agricultural goods. A contemporaneous commander account gives mixed public-health and technical explanations; the evidence does not isolate each factor’s contribution.

historical.duration_note: No supported continuous operational interval for the stated scope.
